\noindent\footnotesize Reproduce the \(n=4\) JIT O1 selected-flow entry with the following generation and timing commands.
\begin{lstlisting}[language=bash,basicstyle=\ttfamily\tiny,breaklines=true,breakatwhitespace=true]
env PYTHONPATH=src dependencies/.venv/bin/python -m pyamplicol generate-process --model assets/models/json/sm/sm.json 'd d~ > z g g g' docs/.z_performance_ufo_sm_outputs/manual/n4/jit_o1 --replace --n_cores 5 --color-accuracy lc --batch-size 64 --symbolica-n-cores 5 --symbolica-output-chunk-size 128 --symbolica-output-chunk-strategy uniform --symbolica-stage-local-parameter-layout --symbolica-iterations 10 --symbolica-max-horner-scheme-variables 1000 --symbolica-max-common-pair-cache-entries 5000000 --symbolica-max-common-pair-distance 1000 --lc-sector-ids 0 --reference-color-order 2,4,5,6,1,3 --symbolica-evaluator-backend jit --symbolica-jit-optimization-level 1
env PYTHONPATH=src dependencies/.venv/bin/python -m pyamplicol time-process --target-runtime 10 --batch-size 64 --json docs/.z_performance_ufo_sm_outputs/manual/n4/jit_o1
\end{lstlisting}
\par\smallskip
\noindent\footnotesize \PAC\ model source: \texttt{external UFO/JSON SM}. Here \(n\) is final-state multiplicity. Each block reports generation seconds and wall/evaluator microseconds per point: one selected flow with the helicity sum on the left, all flows at one fixed helicity on the right. Wall measures Rusticol's public \texttt{evaluate} call; eval separately profiles evaluator plus input packing.  Both use batch 64, stage-local inputs, ten Horner iterations, and a ten-second timing target; output chunks are 128 selected and 8192 all-flow. The green O1 row is the measured default: repeated O3 timings showed no significant Z-family gain.  ASM remains a scalar AArch64 diagnostic.  The driver keeps generated artifacts under \texttt{docs/.z\_performance\_ufo\_sm\_outputs}.  In this external-model table, each \texttt{vs blt-in} entry is the adjacent generation- or wall-time ratio to the matching built-in-SM row at the same multiplicity, backend, and flow/helicity workload; values below one mean that the external model is faster.
